setup.title: Set up nexbooks
setup.text: The first account runs this server: it invites people and may change every setting. It does not see what the others read and hear.
setup.codeHint: It stands in the server log (docker logs nexbooks), or set NEXBOOKS_SETUP_TOKEN.

login.title: Sign in
login.passwordOff: Sign-in with a password is turned off here. Only the operator can still use it.

code.title: Second factor
code.text: The code from your app, or a recovery code.
code.label: Code from the app
code.hint: Six digits. Or one of your recovery codes.
code.textPasskey: Sign in with your passkey, or give a recovery code.

invite.title: Invitation
invite.text: You are invited to nexbooks. Make yourself an account. Your progress and your lists stay closed to everybody else.
invite.invalidText: This invitation no longer works: it was used, has run out or was withdrawn. Ask for a new one.
invite.noWay: Sign-in with a password is off and no sign-in provider is set up. Ask the operator.
invite.haveAccount: This link is for a new account. You are signed in as {{name}} already and do not need it.

remember.label: Stay signed in on this device

remember.ends_one: Until you have not been here for {{count}} day.
remember.ends_other: Until you have not been here for {{count}} days.

setup2fa.scan: Scan the code with an authenticator app, or type in the key. Then the code the app shows.
setup2fa.passkeyLater: Rather without an app? You can add a passkey afterwards under My account → Security.

codes.title: Your recovery codes
codes.text: Each one signs you in once, when the phone is not at hand. They are shown only now: keep them apart from the phone.

forgot.title: Forgot your password

forgot.label: Name or mail address

reset.invalidText: This link does not work any more: it was used or has run out. Ask for a new one, or tap "Forgot your password?" when signing in.
reset.doneText: You can sign in with the new password now.

mail.oldTold: We told the old address about the change.

about.fontsText: nexbooks brings its fonts along, so that opening it asks no other server.

dataFrom.title: Data from the internet
dataFrom.text: What nexbooks asks the internet about books and authors comes from these sources. Each can be switched off on its own under Settings, Sources.

items.openlibrary: a project of the Internet Archive, open data about books.
items.wikidata: the descriptions are CC0, the photos of authors carry their photographer and licence.
items.apple: the best-seller chart, a free feed by Apple.
items.hardcover: with the operator's own token. Hardcover's API terms apply, also for commercial use.
items.audible: only when the operator turns it on, an unofficial interface that nexbooks only reads.
items.bnf: the titles of its language in the works of an author
items.libris: the titles of its language in the works of an author
items.kb: the titles of its language in the works of an author
items.nb: the titles of its language in the works of an author

updates.title: Updates
updates.text: Whether a newer version of nexbooks is out.
updates.dailyHint: Asks GitHub for the newest release when somebody opens this page, once a day at most. Off: only when you press the button.
updates.none: Cannot be checked right now: there is no release yet, or GitHub cannot be reached.
updates.whatGoesOut: Only the question goes out: a request to api.github.com for the newest release of nexbooks, with no names or settings. Besides the sources you switch on (Settings, Sources), the mail server, if you set it up, the push services of the browsers and the sign-in providers when somebody signs in through them, it is the only call nexbooks makes on its own.

profile.text: How the others on this server see you.
profile.displayHintPassword: Empty shows your user name {{name}}; you still sign in with it.
profile.name: Name
profile.hint: A photo from your phone or camera. It is cut to a square, and nothing of the file but the picture is kept: no place, no device.

password.title: Password
password.done: Password changed. Every other device and every connection for e-readers is signed out.

me.setupFirst: The operator requires a second factor. Set it up here, then you can go on.

push.title: Notifications on your devices
push.text: Notices come as a push straight to the phone or into the browser, even while nexbooks is closed. You sign up each device on its own.
push.name: Name of the device
push.ready: Not signed up yet. The browser will ask whether nexbooks may send notifications.
push.denied: The browser blocked notifications for nexbooks. Allow them in the settings of the site (the lock left of the address), then carry on here.
push.insecure: This address has no https, so push does not work. Open nexbooks at its https address.
push.iphone: On the iPhone it only works from the app on the home screen. Put nexbooks there and open it from there.
push.hintHttps: Push needs an address with https (or localhost).
push.hintIphone: On the iPhone it only works from the app on the home screen: Share, then “Add to Home Screen”. From iOS 16.4.
push.deniedNow: Notifications are not allowed. Without them nexbooks cannot send anything.
push.probeHint: Arrives on every device signed up.

devices.title: Signed-in devices
devices.ends_one: A sign-in ends by itself after {{count}} day without use.
devices.ends_other: A sign-in ends by itself after {{count}} days without use.
devices.notify: Tell me about a new sign-in
devices.notifyHint: By push to your devices and by mail: which device, which browser, roughly from where. If it was not you, one tap signs it off.
devices.endedAll: Every other device is signed out.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.text: Sign in with your fingerprint, face or the device's PIN, without password and without code. A passkey counts as two factors by itself and cannot be phished.
passkeys.how: The browser will ask for your fingerprint, face or PIN. The passkey stays on the device or in your keychain.
passkeys.name: Name
passkeys.removeText: Nobody gets in with this passkey afterwards. Delete it on the device too when you no longer need it.
passkeys.unavailable: Passkeys work only over https (or localhost) and in browsers that know them.
passkeys.noAddressOperator: Enter the public address first (<settings>Settings → Sign-in</settings>).
passkeys.noAddressMember: Your operator has to enter the public address first.

oidc.addressOffer: {{provider}} knows you as {{address}}. Should nexbooks take this address?
oidc.addressTaken: The address is your account's now. Confirm it under Profile, then it counts for notices by mail too.

me.keysWait: Devices and API keys work only once you set up a second factor.
me.text: Your profile, your security and your devices.

twofactor.title: Second factor
twofactor.lead: Besides the password, a code from an app on your phone. Recovery codes on paper get you in when the phone is gone.
twofactor.scan: Scan this code with the app, or type the key below into it. Then give the code the app shows, and your password.
twofactor.qr: QR code for the authenticator app
twofactor.passwordHint: Proves it is you at the keyboard.
twofactor.codesLead: Each code signs you in once, when the phone is not at hand. They are shown only now.
twofactor.renewText: The old recovery codes stop working. Give your password to make new ones.
twofactor.disableText: From then on the password alone signs you in. Give it to turn the second factor off.
twofactor.lowCodes: Few recovery codes left. Make new ones while you can still sign in.
twofactor.scanNoPassword: Scan this code with the app, or type the key below into it. Then give the code the app shows.
twofactor.required: It cannot be turned off: the operator requires it for everybody.

invite.noMail: Without a mail server nexbooks sends nothing: copy the link and pass it on yourself.
invite.once: The link works once. It is shown only now.

server.accountsHint: Who uses nexbooks. As the operator you manage accounts and settings; you do not see what people read and hear.
server.inviteText: Whoever follows the link makes an account of their own. Without a mail server you copy the link and pass it on yourself.
server.givePassword: Send a link for a password

promote.text: {{name}} may then change every setting of this server.

demote.text: {{name}} becomes a member and no longer reaches the server's settings.

reset.title: Remove the second factor of {{name}}?
reset.text: For a lost phone: the code from the app, the passkeys and the recovery codes go, every device is signed out, and the person is told. At the next sign-in they set the second factor up again.

signout.title: Sign {{name}} out everywhere?
signout.text: Every device of the account has to sign in again, and the connections for e-readers are deleted.

block.title: Block {{name}}?
block.text: {{name}} no longer gets in, open sessions end at once. Unblocking works at any time.

unblock.title: Unblock {{name}}?
unblock.text: {{name}} can sign in again afterwards, with their own password or through the sign-in provider.

backup_restore.title: Restore this backup?
backup_restore.text: The current state is backed up first. nexbooks restarts, everybody signs in again.

backup_download.title: Download this backup?
backup_download.text: It holds every account and the server's secrets, but no books. It is not encrypted.

backup_upload.title: Upload a backup?
backup_upload.text: The file joins the list of backups. Nothing is restored until you confirm it there.

two_factor_off.title: Stop requiring a second factor?
two_factor_off.text: Then a password alone is enough again to open an account. Whoever has a second factor already keeps it.

link.title: Send {{name}} a link to reset the password?
link.text: The person chooses their password themselves. The link goes by mail to their address when mail is set up, otherwise you get it once to pass on. The second factor stays.

unlink.title: Unlink {{name}}?
unlink.text: {{name}} no longer signs in through {{provider}} afterwards and is told. The account can link itself again when needed.

server.twoFactorRequiredHint: Every account that signs in with a password must set it up before it gets any further. Accounts from the provider bring their own. An account with a password is not affected either when it comes in through a provider for which “{{trusts}}” is on.
server.ownSecondFactorFirst: Set up your own second factor first (My account, Security), or you would be the first one who cannot go on. Not affected is whoever signs in through a provider for which “{{trusts}}” is on.
server.secretKept: stored, leave empty to keep it
server.mailHint: For sending: invitations, "Forgot your password?", confirming mail addresses, the notice of a new sign-in. Without a server the link to copy is enough, and "Forgot your password?" is missing at sign-in.
server.backupsHint: One file with the database, the settings and the server's secrets: accounts, devices, keys, settings. It also holds the key that unseals them (secret.key): with it, the mail credentials, the API keys of the indexers and the passwords of the download programs can be read from the backup. So keep it safe, like a password. Restoring shows a trial run first.
server.uploadedHint: Uploaded. It is in the list now: check it first, then restore.
server.checkOk: Readable: {{accounts}}. Restoring replaces the current state; it is backed up first.
server.checkBad: Damaged: this backup cannot be restored.
server.restarting: nexbooks restarts with the backup. The page reloads in a moment.
server.languagesHint: German and English are built in. Add more as a JSON file; missing texts fall back to English.
server.languageAdded: Language added. It appears under My account, Profile.
server.logHint: What the server did. Without passwords, keys and contents.
server.logClearText: Every line goes. New ones come as before.
server.checkNewer: This backup comes from a newer version of nexbooks. Update nexbooks first, then restore.

push.title: Web Push
push.text: So that notices reach the phone and the browser: of a new sign-in, of a second factor that was reset or an account that was unlinked from a sign-in provider. Operators also hear when a restore fails. Set up from the start; each person signs up their devices under My account.
push.contactHint: The services of Google, Apple and Mozilla ask for an address where they reach the operator. It stands in every message, nothing else of yours.
push.keysText: nexbooks made a key pair of its own. Making a new one signs every device off; each person has to sign them up again.
push.renewText: Every device is signed off. Each person has to sign them up again under My account, Devices and apps.
push.renewed: New key pair made. Every device is signed off.
push.hostsHint: Messages go only to the services of Google, Mozilla, Apple and Microsoft. If a browser needs another one, enter its host here, one per line, such as push.example.com.
push.out: What goes out: an encrypted message to the push service of each browser. Only the device can read it. It never holds anything a person stored.

server.linkSent: The link for {{name}} went to {{email}}. It works once and for 24 hours.
server.linkShown: The link for {{name}}, shown only now, valid once and for 24 hours. Pass it on, the person chooses the password themselves:

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.text: Programs read with a key that each person makes under My account. Here you allow that and see every key, never the key itself.
apiKeys.allowHint: Off: nobody can make keys, and existing ones stop working.
apiKeys.blockText: It stops working at once, for good. The account sees it blocked in its list.
apiKeys.offHint: A key only reads and never does more than its account may.

ereaders.title: E-readers
ereaders.text: Everybody makes connections for their reading apps and their Kobo under My account and sends books to their Kindle. Here you switch that on or off and see every connection, never its password.
ereaders.allowHint: Off: nobody can make connections, send books to a Kindle or put books on the list for the Kobo, and existing connections stop working.
ereaders.blockText: It stops working at once, for good. The account sees it blocked in its list.
ereaders.deleteText: The block is lifted by it, and {{account}} can make a connection of this kind again. This cannot be taken back.

interface.title: Interface
interface.text: Everything the web app can do works through /api/v1 as well. Helpers and programs of your own build on it.
interface.schemaText: OpenAPI, for tools and code generators
interface.authText: device or key in the header of every request; they need no password and no session
interface.limits: Limit per key: 120 requests a minute. Wrong keys count like wrong passwords.

remove.title: Delete {{name}}?
remove.text: The account of {{name}} will be deleted.
remove.typeName: To confirm, type the account name {{name}}
remove.cannotUndo: The account, its sessions, devices, keys and progress are lost and cannot be brought back. The books stay where they lie.

restorePreview.revivedDevices_one: Restoring makes {{count}} device valid again that was locked out or removed since the backup.
restorePreview.revivedDevices_other: Restoring makes {{count}} devices valid again that were locked out or removed since the backup.
restorePreview.revivedKeys_one: Restoring makes {{count}} key valid again that was blocked since the backup.
restorePreview.revivedKeys_other: Restoring makes {{count}} keys valid again that were blocked since the backup.
restorePreview.revivedLinks_one: Restoring makes {{count}} connection for e-readers valid again that was blocked or deleted since the backup.
restorePreview.revivedLinks_other: Restoring makes {{count}} connections for e-readers valid again that were blocked or deleted since the backup.

server.sizeNote: The backup is made while nexbooks runs, through SQLite's own backup function, nothing stalls. Download, delete and restore ask for your password.
server.backupNoBooksText: It holds the database, the settings and the secrets of the server. The book folders belong in your usual file backup, nexbooks reads them and tidies them only on request (Settings, Tidying).

errors.account_locked: Too many wrong tries. The account waits a quarter of an hour.
errors.address_invalid: This address does not work. It has to start with http:// or https://, without a user, password or question mark.
errors.api_off: The operator has not switched API keys on.
errors.avatar_not_a_picture: This is not a picture nexbooks takes (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, HEIC or AVIF).
errors.avatar_too_large: The picture is too large, at most {{max_mb}} MB.
errors.backup_damaged: The backup is damaged. Nothing was changed.
errors.backup_invalid: This is not a nexbooks backup.
errors.backup_too_large: The backup unpacks to more than a backup may hold. Nothing was changed.
errors.backup_too_new: The backup comes from a newer version of nexbooks. Nothing was changed.
errors.bad_preference: nexbooks does not offer this value.
errors.busy: nexbooks is busy right now. Try again in a moment.
errors.cannot_delete_self: You cannot delete your own account.
errors.cannot_demote_self: You cannot take the operator role from yourself.
errors.cannot_join: These two cannot be joined: the books of the library speak against it.
errors.client_address_refused: The program refuses the address of nexbooks. Allow it in the program's whitelist (Transmission: rpc-whitelist).
errors.client_blocked: nexbooks may not ask this address.
errors.client_category_failed: The category could not be made or used in the program.
errors.client_category_missing: NZBGet does not know the category “{{category}}”. Make it in NZBGet (Settings, Categories) and test again. nexbooks does not write to the settings of NZBGet.
errors.client_category_unusable: The program handles this category in a way nexbooks cannot follow. With SABnzbd: job folders on, sorting off.
errors.client_host_refused: SABnzbd refuses the name nexbooks asks under. Add it to the host whitelist of SABnzbd.
errors.client_required: The request did not say which tab it came from. Reload the page.
errors.client_timeout: The program did not answer in time.
errors.client_unreachable: The program cannot be reached. Are address and port right?
errors.client_wrong_kind: Something answers at this address, but not the chosen program.
errors.display_name_invalid: A display name cannot hold control or invisible characters.
errors.display_name_taken: Another account goes by this name.
errors.display_name_too_long: The display name is too long, at most 80 characters.
errors.duration_not_allowed: This duration is not possible here.
errors.indexer_answer_too_large: The answer of the indexer is larger than 10 MB and was refused.
errors.indexer_blocked: nexbooks may not ask this address.
errors.indexer_daily_limit: The limit of this indexer for today is reached. It goes on tomorrow.
errors.indexer_share_used: Your share of the requests to this indexer is used up for today. It goes on tomorrow.
errors.indexer_from_prowlarr: This indexer comes from Prowlarr. Change or remove it there.
errors.indexer_key_rejected: The indexer refuses the API key.
errors.indexer_limit_reached: The indexer reported its request limit. nexbooks asks again in {{retry_after}} seconds.
errors.indexer_not_newznab: Something answers at this address, but not a Newznab or Torznab indexer.
errors.indexer_switched_off: The indexer is switched off where it comes from. Switch it on again in Prowlarr.
errors.indexer_timeout: The indexer did not answer in time.
errors.indexer_unreachable: The indexer cannot be reached. Are address and port right?
errors.indexer_wrong_kind: The answer does not fit the chosen kind: Newznab is for Usenet, Torznab for torrents.
errors.internal_error: Something went wrong on the server.
errors.invalid_account_name: A sign-in name has 2 to 64 characters: letters without accents, digits, dot, hyphen or underscore, no spaces.
errors.invalid_days: Choose one of the offered lifetimes.
errors.invalid_email: This is not a mail address.
errors.key_required: The address changed. Enter the key again: the saved one is never sent to another place.
errors.members_changed: Somebody changed the rights in the meantime. The list is reloaded, look at it and try again.
errors.invite_invalid: This invitation is no longer valid.
errors.issuer_invalid: This is not an OpenID Connect provider.
errors.locale_unusable: This language file cannot be used.
errors.log_level_from_environment: The level is fixed in the environment (NEXBOOKS_LOG_LEVEL).
errors.mail_failed: The mail server did not take the mail.
errors.mail_off: No mail server is set up.
errors.not_found: Not found, or not open to you.
errors.oidc_account: This account signs in through the provider.
errors.operator_network: The operator's settings can be reached from the home network only.
errors.operator_only: Only the operator may do this.
errors.origin_refused: The API is for programs, not web pages.
errors.own_second_factor_first: Set up your own second factor first, on your account page.
errors.password_login_off: Sign-in with a password is turned off.
errors.password_mismatch: The two new passwords are not the same.
errors.password_too_short: The password is too short, at least 12 characters.
errors.provider_first: Set up a sign-in provider first, or nobody but you gets in any more.
errors.prowlarr_blocked: nexbooks may not ask this address.

ready.title: Ready for the internet?
ready.text: Many reach nexbooks from on the road too. nexbooks checks this itself, every time you open the page.

https.title: Public address with https
https.warn: {{address}} has https, but this request came without. Open nexbooks under that address, or let the proxy send X-Forwarded-Proto and name it in NEXBOOKS_TRUSTED_PROXIES.
https.bad: Without https, passwords travel the network in the clear, and Web Push and passkeys do not work at all. Enter the public address with https below.

two_factor.title: Second factor for everybody
two_factor.ok: Whoever signs in with a password needs a code or a passkey as well.
two_factor.bad: Off: a guessed or stolen password is enough to open an account. Turn on "Require a second factor" below.

own_account.title: Your own account
own_account.bad: Has no second factor yet, and it may change everything. Set it up under My account, Security.

brake.title: Protection against guessing
brake.ok: After 5 wrong tries a 15 minute pause, per account and per address. Every try is in the log.
brake.warn: All visitors come through a proxy nexbooks does not know: the pause holds per account, per address only roughly. See “Behind the proxy”.
brake.bad: The list of trusted proxies holds public networks ({{networks}}). Anybody could then make up the sender's address, and the pause after wrong tries no longer holds. List only the address of your proxy.
brake.broken: The protection against guessing fails its own test. Restart nexbooks; if that does not help, please report it.

cookies.title: Sessions and cookies
cookies.ok_one: Cookies only over https and not readable by scripts; a sign-in runs out after {{count}} day without use.
cookies.ok_other: Cookies only over https and not readable by scripts; a sign-in runs out after {{count}} days without use.
cookies.warn: Without https the sign-in cookies travel in the clear. Over https nexbooks protects them by itself.
cookies.bad: NEXBOOKS_COOKIE_SECURE is off: the cookies go unprotected even over https. Set it to auto.

proxy.title: Behind the proxy
proxy.ok: The visitors' real address arrives (proxy {{proxies}} entered as trusted). Without that the protection against guessing would see everybody as one.
proxy.direct: The visitors arrive directly, without a proxy in between.
proxy.warn: The requests come through a proxy ({{proxy}}) that is not entered as trusted: the protection against guessing sees everybody as one. Set NEXBOOKS_TRUSTED_PROXIES to its address.
proxy.bad: Public networks are listed as trusted ({{networks}}). Set NEXBOOKS_TRUSTED_PROXIES to the address of your proxy, not to the whole internet.

secrets.title: Server secrets
secrets.ok: The key for the OIDC secret and the mail password can be read by the owner only.
secrets.env: The key comes from NEXBOOKS_SECRET_KEY, not from a file.
secrets.bad: The file {{path}} can be read by others too (mode {{mode}}). Set it to 600, the owner only.

backups.title: Backup
backups.ok: An automatic backup is on. The books themselves belong in your server's own backup.
backups.warn: No automatic backup. Turn it on under Settings, Backup.

mail.title: Mail address
mail.text: For "Forgot your password?" and notices such as a new sign-in. A new address counts only after you open the link in the mail sent to it.
mail.sent: Link sent. Until you open it, the old address stays.
mail.off: The operator has not set up a mail server yet, so no link can be sent.
mail.passwordHint: For safety: the address is the way back into the account.
mail.passwordFirst: Enter the password above for that

looks.title: Light or dark
looks.libraryText: How the books stand in your library.

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.text: For your own scripts or nexdeck. A key can only read, never change settings.
apiKeys.off: The operator has not allowed API keys.
apiKeys.offForOperator: API keys are not allowed yet.
apiKeys.enableText: After that every person on this server can make keys under My account. A key lets a program only read, never more than the account that made it may. You can switch this off again under Settings, API at any time; keys that exist stop working then too.
apiKeys.name: Name
apiKeys.lifetimeHint: A key that never runs out is the one nobody remembers when it falls into the wrong hands. A year is usually enough; the list shows a week ahead that it runs out.
apiKeys.docs: Everything the web app can do works through the interface under /api/v1 as well. The description is at /api/v1/docs.

ereaders.title: E-readers
ereaders.text: Get books onto your reading device or into your reading app. You see an access once; afterwards only its first characters.
ereaders.off: The operator has switched e-readers off.
ereaders.offOperator: Under Settings, API you switch them on again.
ereaders.safe: Everything here is for your account only. A connection never sees more than you see in nexbooks. Signing out everywhere or a new password deletes all connections.

kindle.title: Kindle
kindle.text: Send books to your Kindle by mail or through Amazon.
kindle.hint: You find it at Amazon, where you manage your content and devices, under your Kindle. Leave it empty to remove the address.
kindle.tested: The test mail is on its way. It holds a small book and shows up in your Kindle library once Amazon knows the sender.
kindle.mail: This server mails books from {{sender}}. Allow this sender at Amazon in the list of approved senders for personal documents, or Amazon throws the mail away. At most {{mb}} MB a book.
kindle.noMail: This server cannot send mail. "Send to Kindle" then downloads the book and opens Amazon's Send to Kindle page in a new tab. Drop the file there, up to 200 MB.
kindle.only: Only an EPUB without copy protection goes. nexbooks converts nothing.

opds.title: Catalogue for reading apps (OPDS)
opds.text: For KOReader, Librera, Moon+ Reader and other apps that speak OPDS.
opds.how: Make a connection of its own for each reading app. It gets a user name, a password and the address of the catalogue. The catalogue shows only e-books you can also see in nexbooks.
opds.name: Name of the connection
opds.namePlaceholder: e.g. Reading app in the living room
opds.shownOnce: Connection "{{name}}". You see the access only now:
opds.passwordHint: Enter all three in your reading app under OPDS catalogue. The password is for the catalogue only, not for your account.

kosync.title: Reading progress for KOReader
kosync.text: Keeps your place in your books the same in KOReader and in nexbooks.
kosync.how: Make a connection of its own for each device that runs KOReader. Your place is kept in e-books in the EPUB format from your libraries, and it has to be the same file: the best way is to fetch the book to the device through the catalogue (OPDS). Only you see your place.
kosync.name: Name of the connection
kosync.namePlaceholder: e.g. Kobo in the living room
kosync.shownOnce: Connection "{{name}}". You see the access only now:
kosync.passwordHint: In KOReader open the top menu and choose Progress sync, then Custom sync server, and enter the address without a slash at the end. Then log in with the user name and the password (Login, not Register) and set the document matching method to Binary. The password is for the sync only, not for your account.

kobo.title: Kobo
kobo.betaHint: Still in beta: this connection has not been tried on a real Kobo yet. If something does not work, please say so on GitHub.
kobo.text: Put books you picked on your Kobo and keep your reading place in step.
kobo.how: Make a connection of its own for each Kobo. Only the books you pick with "To the Kobo" on the page of a book go to it, as EPUB, with nothing converted. Your reading place is kept in step. The Kobo store and the other services of Kobo do not work while the Kobo points at nexbooks. Take the line out again and they work again. If nexbooks runs behind a proxy that handles https, it needs the setting NEXBOOKS_PUBLIC_URL or NEXBOOKS_TRUSTED_PROXIES, or the Kobo is handed addresses with http.
kobo.proxyWarning: You see nexbooks over https, but nexbooks itself assumes {{seen}}. The Kobo would be handed addresses with http, and they hold its password. Set NEXBOOKS_PUBLIC_URL to the address you use, or put your proxy in NEXBOOKS_TRUSTED_PROXIES.
kobo.name: Name of the connection
kobo.namePlaceholder: e.g. Kobo in the living room
kobo.shownOnce: Connection "{{name}}". You see the address only now. It holds the password of the connection, so do not pass it on:
kobo.line: Line for the settings file of the Kobo
kobo.passwordHint: Plug the Kobo into your computer and open the file .kobo/Kobo/Kobo eReader.conf on the device (the folder is hidden). Find the section [OneStoreServices] there and put in the line from above, replacing the line api_endpoint=. Eject the Kobo and restart it. At the next sync the books on your list arrive. The password is for the Kobo only, not for your account.

kobo.added: On your list for the Kobo. The Kobo fetches the book at its next sync.
kobo.removed: Taken off the list. The Kobo removes the book at its next sync.
kobo.noConnection: You have not connected a Kobo yet.

kindle.noAddress: Set the address of your Kindle first.
kindle.byHand: The book is downloading, and Amazon's Send to Kindle page is open in a new tab. Drop the file there.

devices.text: A phone, an app or a script speaks for your account with a token of its own. You see the token only once.
devices.name: Name of the device
devices.shownOnce: This is the token for {{name}}. Copy it now, nexbooks does not show it again.

appConnect.title: Connect the iPhone app
appConnect.sub: Scan the code with the nexbooks app or with the camera of the iPhone.
appConnect.qr: QR code for connecting the iPhone app
appConnect.orType: Or type this code in the app:
appConnect.left_one: The code is good for {{count}} more minute.
appConnect.left_other: The code is good for {{count}} more minutes.
appConnect.closeHint: If you close this window, the code stops working.
appConnect.connectedHint: The device now stands under Device tokens, where you can disconnect it at any time.
appConnect.copyFailed: Copying did not work. Press and hold the code and choose Copy.
appConnect.openHint: If nothing opens, the app is not installed yet. Then type the code in the app.
appConnect.local: The iPhone cannot reach this address. Enter the address from outside in the settings.

deviceCode.button: Connect a device with a code
deviceCode.title: Connect a device with a code
deviceCode.sub: Type the code the device shows, for example an Apple TV.
deviceCode.warningFirst: Only type a code here that you see yourself on your own television.
deviceCode.what: The device then sees everything you see in nexbooks. You can disconnect it at any time under Device tokens.
deviceCode.warning: Confirm only if you see this code on the screen of the device yourself right now. If somebody told you the code, you might connect a stranger's device to your account.
deviceCode.connectedHint: The device now stands under Device tokens, where you can disconnect it at any time.
deviceCode.expired: The code has run out. Have the device show a new code.

pairing.title: Withdraw the code?
pairing.text: The code stops working, also for an app that is scanning it right now. You can show a new code at any time.

deviceRequest.title: Withdraw the confirmation?
deviceRequest.text: The device then gets no access and has to show a new code. If it has fetched the access already, disconnect it under Device tokens.

device.title: Remove {{name}}?
device.text: The device can no longer sign in afterwards. The token cannot be brought back, but you can make a new one at any time.
device.textBrought_one: {{names}}, which this device connected, goes with it. Neither can sign in afterwards. The tokens cannot be brought back, but you can make new ones at any time.
device.textBrought_other: {{names}}, which this device connected, go with it. None of them can sign in afterwards. The tokens cannot be brought back, but you can make new ones at any time.

apiKey.title: Delete the key?
apiKey.text: Programs with the key "{{name}}" can no longer reach nexbooks afterwards. This cannot be undone.

koboRemove.title: Take it off the Kobo?
koboRemove.text: "{{title}}" leaves your list and is deleted from the Kobo at its next sync. You can put it on the Kobo again at any time.

ereaderLink.title: Delete the connection?
ereaderLink.text: The device or reading app with the connection "{{name}}" can no longer get in afterwards. This cannot be undone.

session.title: End the session?
session.text: The browser of this session is signed out afterwards and has to sign in again.

pushDevice.title: Remove the device?
pushDevice.text: "{{name}}" gets no more notifications afterwards until it signs up again.

invite.title: Withdraw the invitation?
invite.text: The link of the invitation stops working. A new invitation is always possible.

locale.title: Remove the language?
locale.text: The uploaded language "{{name}}" is deleted. Whoever chose it sees the default language afterwards.

avatar.title: Remove the profile picture?
avatar.text: The picture is deleted. You can upload a new one at any time.

logoutOthers.title: Sign out everywhere else?
logoutOthers.text: All other browsers, paired devices and connections for e-readers are signed out afterwards. You can connect them again at any time. The list for the Kobo stays.

mailPending.title: Withdraw the new mail address?
mailPending.text: The link sent to {{address}} stops working. You can enter the address again at any time and have a new link sent.

mailAddress.title: Remove the mail address?
mailAddress.text: The address {{address}} is deleted. Without an address there is no link to reset the password and no notices by mail. You can enter a new one later.

oidcLink.title: Unlink the account?
oidcLink.text: Afterwards you no longer sign in with {{name}} but with your password. The link can be made again later.

storage.title: Storage
storage.text: What the data folder holds and where it lies.
storage.network: The data folder lies on a network share
storage.networkText: SQLite can lose data there. Keep the data folder on a local disk. The books may lie on a share.
storage.booksNote: nexbooks does not count the books: they lie in the folders of your libraries, and nexbooks reads them and tidies them only on request (Settings, Tidying).

manifest.description: Your e-books and audiobooks, self-hosted: read, listen, discover.

libraries.title: Libraries
libraries.text: Folders of books that nexbooks reads. The files stay where they are unless you turn tidying on.
libraries.scanText: How often nexbooks looks through the folders by itself. Only what is new or has changed is read.
libraries.empty: No library yet. Make one below.
libraries.noRoots: This server allows no libraries: NEXBOOKS_LIBRARY_ROOTS is empty.
libraries.addText: Choose a folder below {{roots}}. nexbooks reads it right away and touches no file in it.
libraries.name: Name
libraries.rescanText: nexbooks opens every file once more and judges all the books by today's rules, also those that did not change. It takes as long as the first reading did. What people fixed by hand (corrections, matches, "Leave it") stays, and so do reading progress and bookmarks. The files themselves are not touched.
libraries.membersText: Who sees the books of this library. With “Acquire” somebody may also have books fetched. With “Manage” somebody may also scan and see the problems. As the operator you see books only if you are one of them yourself.

aborted.offline: The folder cannot be reached. Nothing was marked as gone.
aborted.empty: The folder holds no book, but nexbooks knows books in it. Nothing was marked as gone. Is the share mounted?
aborted.truncated: The folder holds more entries than nexbooks looks at in one run. What it saw was read, nothing was marked as gone.
aborted.error: The last run failed. The log says more.

libraries.deferred_one: {{count}} file was still being written and comes in the next run.
libraries.deferred_other: {{count}} files were still being written and come in the next run.
libraries.problemsShow: {{count}} files could not be read. Show

reason.unreadable: The file is damaged, or not what its name says.
reason.unsupported: nexbooks does not read this kind of file.
reason.too_large: The file, or a part of it, is larger than allowed.
reason.too_many_entries: The e-book holds more files than a book can have.
reason.zip_bomb: The e-book unpacks to far more than it weighs.
reason.timeout: Reading the file took too long.
reason.crashed: The reader crashed while reading the file.
reason.changed: The file changed while it was read.
reason.bad_name: The name is not valid text, so it was left out. Rename it to read it.
reason.failed: nexbooks failed to handle this file. The log says why.

libraries.removeText: nexbooks forgets this library and everything it learned about its books, including the reading progress, the bookmarks and the reading stack of everybody who reads in it. This cannot be undone. The files stay where they are, nothing is deleted, and the wish lists stay as they are. If you add the folder again later, nexbooks reads it anew, but progress, bookmarks and the reading stack start from the beginning.

texts.hardcover: Works in many languages, series and the place in them. Needs a token of the server's own.

procure.title: Acquisition
procure.text: Where nexbooks gets books from and how: indexers, download programs, formats, automation and rights. For the operator only. About using it: nexbooks comes with no indexers and no sources. You add them yourself and are responsible for loading only what you may use. nexbooks never gets around a copy protection: protected books are recognised and turned down.

start.title: Setting up fetching
start.notice: nexbooks comes with no indexers and no sources. You add them yourself and are responsible for loading only what you may use. nexbooks never gets around a copy protection: protected books are recognised and turned down.
start.audible: Audible knows the running time of an audiobook. With it nexbooks tells abridged and wrong versions apart by itself, and Discover shows the audiobook lists “New releases” and “Coming soon”. It also shows the gaps in your series and more of your authors then (a Hardcover token does that as well). nexbooks only reads the catalogue, slowly, and sends only a title, an author and a market. Audible does not offer this interface officially. Without Audible everything else goes on, but nexbooks asks you about every audiobook it loaded whether it is the unabridged version.
start.foot: You can change this any time under Settings, Sources. If you close this window, nexbooks asks again later.

auto.heading: Automation
auto.text: With automation nexbooks searches every wish by itself, loads the best release that fits, checks the file and puts the book on the shelf.

main.title: Automation
main.text: The main switch. When it is off, nexbooks only searches when somebody presses “Search now”.

rss.title: New releases
rss.text: At this rhythm nexbooks reads the newest entries of the indexers (RSS). That is how it finds books that came out today without searching for each one.
rss.label: RSS every
rss.share: {{name}}: paused until tomorrow. Half of the daily limit is used up for reading; the other half stays for searches.

retry.title: Search again
retry.text: Wishes that found nothing are searched again after this time. Wishes for books that are not out yet wait until the day they come out.
retry.label: Search again every

limits.title: Daily limit per indexer
limits.text: Many indexers lock you out after a number of requests a day. nexbooks keeps to the limit and waits until the next day. 0 means no limit.
limits.label: Daily limit {{name}}
limits.suggest: The indexer reports {{max}} requests a day.
limits.reset: The count starts again at {{time}} (midnight of the instance). Searches and the reading of new entries count; downloads are counted apart. What nexbooks does by itself (wishes that come back, new entries, better formats) uses at most 70 percent of the limit. The rest is kept for new wishes and “Search now”.

replace.title: Replacement after a failure
replace.text: If a download fails or does not pass the check, nexbooks blocks the release and takes the next one.
replace.hint: The release goes on the block list and the search goes on.

seed.title: Torrents
seed.text: From the start the torrent leaves the program as soon as the book is filed. You can have it shared further.
seed.label: Seed until
seed.hint: With “not at all” the torrent goes at once, even when the tracker asks for a ratio or a minimum time. Private trackers often do: choose one of the other two then.

retention.title: Usenet: age of releases
retention.text: How old a Usenet release may be at most. Older ones are no longer on the news servers and would fail in the program.
retention.label: Maximum age in days
retention.hint: 0 means: nexbooks reads the retention from the news servers of the programs (SABnzbd, NZBGet). Where they report none, there is no limit.
retention.read: The programs report {{days}} days at the moment.
retention.readNone: The programs report no limit at the moment.

text.no_space: Make room and have it checked again, or cancel the download.

text.paused: Once it goes on in the program, this note goes by itself. If you do not want to wait, block the release and nexbooks looks for another one, or cancel the download.

text.runtimeLong: It may be a bundle or another book. You decide.
text.runtimeUnproven: Without a running time from a catalogue (Audible, for example) and without a word in the names, nexbooks does not know which version this is. If it is the unabridged reading, keep it. You decide.
text.runtimeShorter: That is 5 to 20 percent short. It may be abridged, a part may be missing, or it is another reading. Listen and decide.
text.runtimeDramatized: Several voices or the catalogue point to a radio play, not a reading of the book. You decide.

text.bundleAny: Choose the wished book. nexbooks throws the others away.

text.files_unassigned: Title or author in the files do not fit the wished book. File it anyway if it is the right one.
text.language_unclear: What the file says contradicts itself, so nexbooks blocked nothing. If the book is in {{wanted}}, file it.
text.language_unknown: Neither the files nor the name of the release, its folder or the category of the indexer name a language. If the book is in {{wanted}}, file it.
text.place_failed: {{reason}} The files are still in the download folder. Check the goal and check again.
text.upgrade_position_page: {{OldArticle}} {{old}} has fixed pages, {{nowArticle}} {{now}} does not. You were on page {{page}}. nexbooks set you to about {{percent}} %, a position in flowing text, not an exact one.

text.partial: The title names a part, such as part 1. File it if it is the whole book.
text.pen_name: It may be a pen name, a translator or a reader where the author belongs, or a slip in the name. File it if it is the book wished.

text.works_joined: While reading the libraries, nexbooks took two entries that were on the shelf already for one book and put them together. If they are two books, split them again.
text.duplicate: nexbooks deletes none of it. If it is the same, put one edition in the trash on the page of the book. Otherwise tap Got it.

block.count_other: {{count}} blocked releases. nexbooks takes them in no search.

why.other_language: The release was in another language than the one wished.
why.format_not_wanted: The format is not ticked in the ranking.
why.dangerous: The release held a program or script.
why.archive_unsupported: The release was an archive nexbooks does not unpack.
why.not_better: The release was not better than the format there is.

dialog.title: Acquire
dialog.sub: nexbooks looks for it, loads it, checks it and puts the book on your shelf.
dialog.languageHint: The languages allowed are the ones under Settings, Acquisition, Formats and place, Languages.

noIndexer.title: No indexer is set up yet.
noIndexer.operator: Without an indexer nexbooks cannot search. Set one up first.
noIndexer.member: Ask the operator to set up an indexer. Until then the book stays on your wish list.

dialog.haveBoth: Both versions are on your shelf already.
dialog.allRunning: Everything is under way for this book: the missing versions are on the shelf or wished.
dialog.proposal: The place by kind is not writable. nexbooks proposes “{{library}}”.
dialog.readOnlyOther: {{why}} Choose a library that is writable.
dialog.readOnlyAll: {{why}} None of your libraries is writable. The wish waits until nexbooks may write somewhere.
dialog.notOutText: The wish waits until then and searches by itself.

manual.title: The automatic work is off.
manual.text: The wish is made, but nothing is searched until you start it.

hint.have: The {{kind}} is on your shelf already.

dialog.unwritableList: Greyed out because nexbooks may not write there: {{list}}.
dialog.chooseLibrary: Several libraries take this kind of book. Choose where it goes. The operator can set one under Acquisition, Place.

done.waiting: nexbooks waits for the day it comes out.

entry.wishNote: Acquire them one by one or all at once.
entry.wishNoRight: Your wish list. Only who has the right to acquire can acquire.

line.upgrade: Looking for an upgrade · has {{have}}, looks for {{goal}}
line.capped: Waiting for the limit of the day

upload.title: Upload books
upload.lead: Drop the files of a book here or choose them. nexbooks checks them and files them into the library like a download. Your own files go in whatever their language, also one not ticked for fetching.
upload.leadWork: Drop the files here or choose them. nexbooks checks them and files them with this book ({{kind}}). Your own files go in whatever their language.
upload.formats: EPUB, PDF, AZW3, MOBI, M4B, MP3, M4A, FLAC; an audiobook also as several files or as a ZIP
upload.mixed: Please upload e-books and audiobooks separately.
upload.wrongKind: The {{kind}} is missing here. The files chosen are something else.
upload.noLibrary: You may not bring books into any library that takes this kind.
upload.done: The book is on the shelf now.
upload.needs: nexbooks needs you for this book. "Needs you" says what to do.

stop.title: Cancel the upload?
stop.text: What was sent already is deleted. This cannot be undone.

rejected.dangerous: There is a program or script among the files. nexbooks takes none of them.
rejected.no_book: nexbooks found no readable book in the files.
rejected.other_kind: The files are not the kind of book that is missing here.
rejected.upload_mixed: The archive holds e-books and recordings together. Upload them separately.
rejected.archive_encrypted: The archive has a password and cannot be opened.
rejected.archive_unsafe: The archive holds paths or links that lead out of its folder.
rejected.archive_too_large: The archive is too large to unpack.
rejected.archive_unsupported: nexbooks does not unpack this kind of archive. ZIP works.
rejected.other: nexbooks did not file the files.

move.title: Move to another library
move.none: No other library you look after takes this edition.
move.noneChoosable: None of the libraries can take the edition right now.
move.preview: This is how the edition will lie in “{{library}}”:
move.what: nexbooks moves {{files}} ({{size}}) in the background. The edition stays the same: place, bookmarks, history, matching and corrections are kept. Nothing is overwritten.
move.copies: That library lies on another drive: nexbooks copies the files, compares their size and only then removes the old ones.
move.sourceReadOnly: nexbooks may not write in “{{source}}” ({{why}}). Without that the old files cannot be removed.
move.busy: This edition is being moved, or one of the libraries is being tidied. Try again in a moment.

confirm.title: Move into “{{library}}”?
confirm.text: The files go from “{{source}}” to “{{target}}”, then nexbooks removes them in “{{source}}”. Whoever may see “{{target}}” will see the edition. Place, bookmarks and history stay. It can be moved back the same way.

state.queued: Waiting until nexbooks is free in the background.

where.source: All files still lie in “{{source}}”, nothing was lost.
where.bothPlace_one: The edition still lies in “{{source}}”. 1 file was left in “{{target}}” that nexbooks could not remove again.
where.bothPlace_other: The edition still lies in “{{source}}”. {{count}} files were left in “{{target}}” that nexbooks could not remove again.
where.bothClear_one: The edition lies in “{{target}}” now. 1 old file is still in “{{source}}”.
where.bothClear_other: The edition lies in “{{target}}” now. {{count}} old files are still in “{{source}}”.

why.no_space: There is not enough room at the target.
why.taken: A file of that name lay at the target already. nexbooks overwrites nothing.
why.target_taken: A file of that name lay at the target already. nexbooks overwrites nothing.
why.source_changed: A file changed since nexbooks read it. Scan the library again, then try once more.
why.target_changed: A file at the target is no longer as nexbooks put it there.
why.source_left: An old file could not be removed.
why.source_not_writable: nexbooks may not write in the library the edition lies in.
why.target_not_writable: nexbooks may not write in the target library.
why.no_write: nexbooks may not write at the target.
why.link: A link lies on the way. nexbooks follows no links.
why.outside: A path leads out of the library.
why.too_long: The path at the target would be too long.
why.gone: The edition or one of the libraries is gone.
why.moved_meanwhile: The edition lies in another library by now.

author.notFound: nexbooks does not know this person.

state.building: nexbooks is asking the sources about the works of {{name}}. This takes a moment; the page fills in by itself.
state.no_source: Without sources nexbooks knows only the books in your libraries. Which sources may be asked is set by the operator in the settings.
state.main_off: Without sources nexbooks knows only the books in your libraries. Which sources may be asked is set by the operator in the settings.
state.failed: The sources did not answer just now. nexbooks will ask again later.
state.refreshing: The sources are being asked again.

note.title: Where this catalogue comes from
note.summaryUnsure: {{sources}} · {{sure}} of {{total}} works recognised for sure, {{unsure}} unsure
note.summaryNoSourceUnsure: {{sure}} of {{total}} works recognised for sure, {{unsure}} unsure
note.thin: Only a few sources know {{name}}, and only for single books. The catalogue may have gaps, above all for announced books.
note.rule: A work stands here when at least two sources know it. Translations hang on the same work; collections and comics stand apart.
note.library: For {{language}} nexbooks asks the national library ({{library}}).
note.footer: What nexbooks cannot place in a kind for sure stands under “Not placed for sure” and is never fetched by itself. As of: {{when}}. The sources are asked again at most once a day.

author.penText: Published under this name. nexbooks lists these books with {{person}} because the sources give both names to the same person.
author.unsureText: nexbooks does not know for sure what kind of book this is. It is never fetched by itself. Move it if you know; nexbooks remembers.

why.comic: A comic or graphic novel; a source may list it as a novel.
why.anthology: With many authors, perhaps a collection.
why.forms: Letters, plays or essays? The sources do not say for sure.
why.short: Very short, perhaps a novella or a story.
why.about: A book about the person or one of their books, perhaps not by them.
why.namesake: Several people share this name. No source proves it is by this person.

author.movedBack: “{{title}}” stands where the sources put it again.

watch.textCan: New books by {{name}} are wished as soon as they are announced and come to the shelf by themselves on the day they come out. What is out already stays as it is; you get that with “Get”.
watch.textList: New books by {{name}} go onto your wish list as soon as they are announced. Only people with the right to get books may do that here.
watch.died: {{name}} died in {{year}}; watching is still worth it for translations and books from the estate.
watch.more: Also non-fiction, children’s books and collections
watch.waiting: nexbooks is fetching the catalogue of {{name}} and then looks at what is announced.
watch.announcedList: Announced and put on your wish list: {{titles}}.
watch.nothing: Nothing is announced at the moment.
watch.notYetCan: “{{title}}” is not announced in {{language}} yet, only in {{other}}; until then it is on your wish list, and nexbooks wishes it as soon as it is.
watch.notYetList: “{{title}}” is not announced in {{language}} yet, only in {{other}}; it is on your wish list.
watch.on_wished_one: You watch {{name}}. {{count}} announced book is wished now.
watch.on_wished_other: You watch {{name}}. {{count}} wishes made for announced books.
watch.on_listed_one: You watch {{name}}. {{count}} book is on your wish list.
watch.on_listed_other: You watch {{name}}. {{count}} books are on your wish list.
watch.more_listed_one: {{count}} more book is on your wish list.
watch.more_listed_other: {{count}} more books are on your wish list.

stopped.no_indexers: No indexer is switched on. nexbooks wishes the announced books as soon as one is.
stopped.share: Watching has made as many wishes today as it may. nexbooks goes on tomorrow.
stopped.list_full: Your wish list is full. nexbooks goes on when there is room again.
stopped.many: That is a lot of books. nexbooks makes the rest in a moment.
stopped.off: The automatic work is switched off. Your watch is saved; nexbooks wishes as soon as it is on again.

watch.offText: nexbooks then wishes no new books by {{name}}. You can switch it on again any time.
watch.offKeep: Wishes and wish list entries already made stay
watch.offKeepText: They go on, and you can take them away one by one under Get.
watch.offRemove: Also take away what has not started yet
watch.offRemoveText: Wishes that are still waiting and books nexbooks put on your wish list go. That cannot be taken back. What is already loading stays.
watch.offDoneKeep: You no longer watch {{name}}. Wishes already made stay.
watch.offDoneRemove: You no longer watch {{name}}. The wishes that had not started are gone.
watch.languageOff: {{language}} is no longer fetched; nexbooks now wishes in {{target}}.
watch.noLanguage: No language is chosen for getting books, so nexbooks wishes nothing.
watch.listedCan: On your wish list instead of wished: {{titles}}.
watch.yearCan: Announced for {{year}}, no day yet: “{{title}}”; nexbooks wishes it as soon as the day is known.
watch.yearList: Announced for {{year}}, no day yet: “{{title}}”; nexbooks puts it on your wish list as soon as the day is known.
watch.fewSources: Books to come are known mostly to Audible and Hardcover, and both are off. So nexbooks sees little of what comes out soon.
watch.paused: The automatic work is switched off. nexbooks wishes nothing until it is on again.
